what_its_for: Acalabrutinib is a cancer medicine used to treat certain types of blood cancers, including chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL), and mantle cell lymphoma (MCL). It works by blocking a protein in cancer cells called BTK, which helps slow or stop the cancer from growing and spreading.
how_to_take: Swallow the capsules whole with a full glass of water. Do not open, break, or chew the capsules. You can take this medicine with or without food. Try to take it at the same times every day to keep steady levels in your body. If you take antacids (like Tums or Maalox), take acalabrutinib at least 2 hours before or after the antacid. If you take a stomach acid reducer called a proton pump inhibitor (like omeprazole or pantoprazole), talk to your doctor as this may affect how well acalabrutinib works.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 100 mg taken twice a day (about 12 hours apart). Your doctor may adjust your dose based on your health, other medicines you take, or any side effects you experience. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is within 3 hours of your scheduled time. If it has been more than 3 hours, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store acalabrutinib at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it in its original container and away from moisture, heat, and direct light. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of unused or expired medicine safely — ask your pharmacist about medication take-back programs.
what_to_avoid: Avoid grapefruit, grapefruit juice, Seville oranges, and starfruit while taking this medicine, as they can increase the amount of drug in your body and raise the risk of side effects. Avoid taking herbal supplements like St. John's Wort, as it can make acalabrutinib less effective. Tell your doctor or dentist before any surgery or dental procedure, since this medicine can increase your risk of bleeding. Avoid contact sports or activities that could cause injury and bleeding. Do not get live vaccines without talking to your doctor first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: unusual or serious bleeding (such as blood in urine or stool, coughing up blood, or bleeding that won't stop), signs of serious infection (fever, chills, severe cough, or painful urination), chest pain, shortness of breath, or fast or irregular heartbeat (signs of heart rhythm problems), severe headache, dizziness, weakness, or vision changes (possible signs of bleeding in the brain), new skin growths or sores that don't heal (possible signs of skin cancer), swollen lymph nodes, night sweats, or worsening symptoms, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or dark urine (liver problems), or severe rash or allergic reaction (hives, swelling of face or throat, difficulty breathing).
when_it_works: Acalabrutinib starts working in your body right away, but you may not feel or see results immediately. Some patients notice improvement in symptoms like fatigue, night sweats, or swollen lymph nodes within the first few weeks to months. Lab tests and imaging scans will help your doctor track how well the medicine is working. It is important to keep taking it every day as prescribed, even if you feel well, unless your doctor tells you to stop.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Acalabrutinib can harm an unborn baby. Women who can become pregnant should use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 1 week after the last dose. Men with female partners who can become pregnant should also use birth control during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine and for at least 2 weeks after the last dose. Older adults (65+): This medicine can be used in older adults but they may be at higher risk for certain side effects like infections and bleeding — your doctor will monitor you closely. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted.
